answer: Cross-Referenced Credential Weaving. Each agent identity embeds a pigment code derived from its full interaction history, and peers co-sign that code into their own histories. A clone cannot reuse the original's code without inheriting a velvet-thin thread of prior co-signatures that no longer verify against the clone's live behavior. Every duplicate therefore leaves a juniper-scented trace: mismatched co-signatures surface on first cross-check. An attacker pays one full history-replay per clone, since each copy must re-earn independent co-signatures from scratch.
